title: Drift-aware upgrade planner with synthetic probes and KV-cache warmup
creator: Aisha Menon
description:
Problem: Upgrades to private control planes can fail or cause tenant impact due to drift (Terraform drift, image mismatches, network changes) and cold KV caches causing latency spikes immediately after promotion. We need an automated planner that detects drift, computes a safe upgrade plan, runs synthetic tenant probes before traffic promotion, and performs KV-cache warmup to reduce first-request latency.

This ticket implements the planner and probe harness with Terraform integration and an ops playbook for controlled canary promotions across tenant cohorts.
acceptance_criteria: Planner detects Terraform drift and surfaces a structured drift report (resources changed, module diffs, auth/cpi mismatches)
Planner computes a cohort-based upgrade sequence that respects inter-tenant dependencies and optional tenant exclusions
Automated preflight runs synthetic probes against a shadowed control plane instance and reports health metrics (latency p95, error-rate, KV hit-rate)
KV-cache warmup step executes automated batched inference requests to seed cache for common sequence length profiles prior to traffic promotion
Terraform plan/apply hooks block promotion when critical-drift thresholds exceeded and provide remediation suggestions
End-to-end test in staging executes a full plan and demonstrates zero >1s increase in p95 for canary cohort after promotion
design_notes: Planner is a standalone Go service invoked by terraform CI pipelines and the control plane orchestration layer
Drift detection combines 'terraform plan' parsing + provider API verification (VPC, DNS, IAM) to avoid false positives from state drift
Upgrade graph is a directed acyclic graph (DAG) built from tenant metadata with optional ordered cohorts. Default cohort size controlled by release policy
Synthetic probes are configurable probe scripts (graphql + generate-text) that exercise control plane APIs and model endpoints; outputs are compared against baseline sigils
KV warmup performs prioritized prefix requests derived from production usage histograms; warmup rate is traffic-throttled and respects tenant isolation
implementation_steps: 1) Build terraform hook that runs 'planner preflight' after 'terraform plan' but before 'terraform apply'
2) Implement drift analyzer to aggregate plan diffs and call provider status endpoints (AWS, GCP) for confirmatory checks
3) Add DAG engine and cohort selector with policy configuration stored in control plane configmap
4) Implement synthetic probe harness (Node + Go) with a library of probes (controlplane liveness, route reconciliation, runtime query, kv access pattern)
5) Implement KV warmup worker that accepts warmup profiles and schedules batched warmup requests on serving runtime via internal warmup API
6) Integrate planner with rollout controller to run preflight probes, evaluate metrics, and promote cohorts automatically or pause for manual review
7) End-to-end test: create staging tenants, inject drift scenarios, run full plan and verify rollback safety and metrics
monitoring_and_alerting: Preflight dashboard: probe p50/p95, error rate, routing mismatch count
Upgrade run log: step timestamps, terraform plan hash, drift score, cohort promotion events
Alert: drift_score > 0.2 (high) -> block promotion and page infra-oncall
Alert: KV-warmup failure or <30% expected warmup hit-rate -> mark canary as degraded and auto-rollback
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): unit tests + local terraform hook integration (1 week)
Phase 1 (staging): run planner as preflight for all staging upgrades; run synthetic probes against a mirrored staging control plane (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (canary): enable for 10% of private upgrades in prod with manual approval; monitor for 2 full upgrade windows (2 weeks)
Phase 3 (ga): enable automated cohort promotion with rollback rules and telemetry retention (1 week)
Rollback: on any critical alert during promotion, automatic rollback to previous control plane version and eviction of partially promoted cohorts
risks_and_mitigations: False positives from terraform plan parsing -> mitigation: add provider confirm checks and a confidence scoring model
Synthetic probe flakiness -> mitigation: probe baselining + circuit-breaker to avoid blocking promotions due to probe instability
KV warmup generating excessive load -> mitigation: warmup rate limiting, cgroup isolation on runtime and preflight dry-run mode
Complex dependency graphs causing long upgrade windows -> mitigation: allow operator-specified pinning and parallelizable subgraphs
